$comment: Geology (systemic terrain T2, ADR 0075): rock types, the strata stacks they form, the rock provinces placing the stacks, and the rule-based shaping of the ground by its rock. Prototype content (ARCHITECTURE.md §6.1): the rocks show today's blocks (stone, sand, dirt) until rocks of their own; their `color` is the Chisel rock overlay's. A rock: hardness 0..1 (hard rock stands as walls and caps, soft rock wastes to talus), jointing `bedded` (breaks along its beds: a step every `bed` m, each a wall and a tread), `vertical` (columns: one sheer wall the unit's height, a tread on top) or `massive` (no joints: rises unstepped), solubility 0..1 (unused yet: karst later), and the blocks it shows: `face` on its walls, `cap` on its treads, `scree` on its talus. A stack: its layers top to bottom, each a rock and a thickness (m), repeating with height from sea level; its `weight` in the provinces (0: never the noise's, only named by a rule such as `plateProvinces`). `provinces`: a stack per region, chosen by a noise of `wavelength` m by the stacks' weights (a biome's `rockStack` takes its place where the biome is). `shaping`: the ground mapped through its stack's profile `strength` 0..1 of the way (0, the default world's: the terrain unchanged), `tread` how wide a hard bed's tread is, `sheer` how narrow a hard wall is (higher: steeper), `treadRelief` 0..0.5 the share of a bed's height its tread rises over (0: dead-flat caps; a little keeps the ground's relief on a mesa top), `ledge` (m) and `ledgeEvery` (share of a bed): a soft bedded rock's slope is ramped runs broken by a near-vertical ledge this tall this often (owner, 2026-11-13: layered steps as ledges, not a field of ½ m stairs), `notched` 1: where the shaping is on (strength > 0) the stored ramps also top columns on diagonal contours (notched ramps), not only straight edges; all read only where strength > 0. `erosion` (systemic terrain T4, rule-based, from the world map's plan view; a biome opts in with `erosion` 0..1 and `gullies` 0..1, absent 0, so the default world is unchanged): drainage lines are the map cells whose flow accumulation is at least `threshold` cells (lower: denser drainage); from each, the scarp has retreated `reach` m × (1 − `resist` × the stack's cap rock's hardness) × (1 + `valley` × log2 of the line's accumulation over the threshold) × (1 ± `outline` noise of `outlineWavelength` m) − `relief` m per m of the hill's height over the floor; nearer than that the land is the floor (the drainage line's height, `snap` 0..1 of the way down to the top of the stack's lowest soft layer), farther it stands, with a wall `wall` m wide at the edge and a talus skirt `talusWidth` m wide rising to `talusShare` of the hill's height. `gullyWavelength` and `gullyDepth`: the badlands' rills (a biome's `gullies`). `strength` scales every biome's `erosion`. The red desert (0.59.0; owner, 2026-11-13: "a red brown sand for the red desert areas"): the red rock mesa's own stack `dwell:red_desert_beds` (weight 0, named by the biome's `rockStack`) is the red beds' sandstone over red siltstone, whose talus and benches show `dwell:red_sand`. Run `node shared/worldgen/gen.mjs` after editing; CI fails on stale output.

rocks.name: dwell:lava_glass
rocks.$comment: Lava quenched where it met the sea (an active volcano's apron, plates.json uplift.volcanism, 0.64): obsidian; in no stack.

arid.$comment: What arid ground is, for a rock's `capBy` (BUGS.md #134; owner, 2026-11-13: "We need a red brown sand for the red desert areas"): the biomes' own climate values, as the red rock mesa's `where` (rain in mm where the world has a climate, any without one; the geography's wetness, 0..1; celsius at least, so a hot desert, not the boreal's or the tundra's dry ground). A rock's `capBy` lists {"<climate>": block} (the code's vocabulary: arid), the first whose climate holds giving its treads' block, else its `cap`: sandstone's treads are red sand where it is arid, red sandstone elsewhere.

blends.name: dwell:mesa_country
blends.$comment: Monument Valley's floors (owner, 2026-11-13): mostly red dirt, red sand on the slopes, washes and patches, paler tan patches blended in; on the red desert beds (the red rock mesa's own stack).

plateProvinces.$comment: The rock provinces from plate history (docs/proposals/REALISTIC_WORLD.md §3.4, phase R5): in a Realistic world (terrain.json tectonics.plates 1) each column's setting on its face's plate layout picks its stack, in place of the provinces' noise. The settings are the code's vocabulary: `arc` (on an arc's cone, within 0.85 of its radius), `hotspot` (on a hotspot chain's island), `accreted` (old seafloor scraped onto the overriding plate: within `accretedWidth` m of a subducting boundary on its overriding side), `core` (the uplifted core: within `coreWidth` m of a collision boundary, or `rangeCore` [near, far] m behind a subducting boundary on the overriding side, the range's crest), `rift` (within `riftWidth` m of a divergent boundary), `basin` (farther than `basinDistance` m from every boundary of the plate: the quiet interior, its beds undisturbed) and `default` (anywhere). `edgeFade` (m, absent 0): the shaping fades in over this far inside the edge of a setting (a cone's rim, a width's line, the plate's boundary), so where the shaping is on (the Realistic world's `geology.shaping.strength`) one province meets the next with no wall along the edge (WORK_QUEUE item 15). `rules`: a setting and the stack it takes (by name), the first rule whose setting holds winning; where none does, the provinces' noise picks. The stacks name their rocks and the rocks their blocks (§7 q5: no new rock blocks yet, so andesite shows basalt, schist and limestone stone, sandstone red sandstone): a later andesite, schist or limestone block replaces one by data alone. Read only where the tectonics come from plates; the default and starter worlds never read it. The shaping (`shaping.strength`) still decides whether the rock's blocks show on the ground; the soils (vegetation.json rockSoils) read the province's rock everywhere. Prototype content. `mixing` (absent: one stack per setting, edges at their widths; WORK_QUEUE item 15, owner 2026-11-13: "horizontal slices of noise"): a rule's `mix` lists other stacks the setting mixes in, each by its `weight` (the rule's own `stack` weighs 1), picked by a noise of `wavelength` m whose sample point is warped `warp` m at `warpWavelength` m, so a plate's interior is patches of several stacks, not one; every boundary distance is shifted by a noise of about ±`edgeShift` m at `edgeWavelength` m, so a setting's edge wanders instead of running parallel to its boundary. The shaping fades in over `fade` m inside a mixed patch's edge (narrower than a setting's `edgeFade`, so most of a patch's ground keeps its steps).

tectonic.$comment: The tectonic rock provinces (systemic terrain T5, terrain.json tectonics): on a volcano (the arc's cones and the hotspot islands) the ground's stack is volcanic, in the overriding plate's old core (coreDistance m behind a convergent boundary) core; elsewhere the provinces' noise picks. Read only when the tectonics are on and the shaping shows rock (strength > 0). snow: the block of the snow line's cover (terrain.json tectonics.snowBelowC; read only when it is on); ice: the glacier's, on gentle ground colder than tectonics.iceBelowC (read only when both are on).
